definition: Annul means to make void or invalid.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word annul. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know annul should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Because the officiant's license had lapsed years before, the county annulled all thirty weddings he had performed that spring.
To contest a result is much milder than to annul it — the challenge questions the result while it goes on standing.
Overturn stops just short of annul: an overturned ruling is reversed going forward, while an annulled one is erased as if it had never been.

To void something is to stamp it no-longer-valid — the ticket, permit, or warranty simply stops counting from that point on. Annul digs deeper: a court declares the thing invalid from the very beginning, as though it had never existed. Voiding kills the future; annulment erases the past too.

Quash is what a court does to a decision, order, or indictment — it forcefully throws the ruling out. Annul aims at the thing itself, a marriage or contract, and declares it void from the start. You quash what another authority decided; you annul what the parties made.

Annul means to make void or invalid.
The land office annulled the deed the moment surveyors proved the seller had never owned the parcel: in law the sale had simply never happened, and the buyer's money came back to the last cent.
Annul goes further than cancel: a canceled deal stops running forward, but an annulled one is declared void from the beginning — treated as though it never existed.
Courts and officials annul marriages, contracts, elections, and results.

The prize commission met in emergency session over the Harlow Medal, awarded three years earlier for a paper on deep-sea vents.
An audit had shown the data was fabricated before the paper was ever submitted; the award had been tainted from its first day.
Suspending the medal going forward, several members argued, would not be enough.
So the commission voted to annul the award altogether: the medal was struck from the rolls, and the record now shows no laureate for that year at all.
The chair put the difference plainly: 'We are not taking the medal away.
We are recognizing that, legally, it was never given.'
